factors.name: Net size
factors.summary: Number of duplicate tasks (0.97), Size (0.97) and Token split (0.95) load very highly, so the factor captures how large a net is in nodes, arcs and repeated labels. Density (-0.58) and Average connector degree (-0.48) load negatively, consistent with larger nets being sparser, but both also cross-load on Factor 3 (and Average connector degree on Factor 2). It is the strongest factor, with 37% explained variance.

factors.name: Connector degree and connectivity
factors.summary: Maximum connector degree (0.95), Coefficient of network connectivity (0.66) and Average connector degree (0.46) load here, so the factor reflects how many arcs meet at connectors and arcs per node. Maximum connector degree dominates and is flagged as a possible Heywood case, and Average connector degree cross-loads on Factors 1 and 3, so the factor rests largely on one measure.

factors.name: Connector homogeneity and density
factors.summary: Connector Heterogeneity loads strongly negatively (-0.93), while Density (0.61) and Average connector degree (0.58) load positively, so nets using a single connector type tend to be denser with higher connector degree in this dataset. Density and Average connector degree cross-load with similar size on Factor 1, which blurs the factor. How undefined heterogeneity values for nets without connectors were handled is not stated.

factors.name: Separability (weak)
factors.summary: Only Separability (0.63) is assigned. Coefficient of network connectivity (0.48), Average connector degree (0.41) and Density (0.40) show moderate loadings that are not assigned because they load more strongly elsewhere. With 11% explained variance and an eigenvalue of 0.71, this factor is weak and possibly an artefact of extracting more factors than suggested.

interpretation.overall: The data are suitable for a factor analysis (Bartlett's test significant, overall KMO 0.75 above 0.6), and the four varimax-rotated factors explain 85% of the variance. A clear size factor dominates, followed by factors for connector degree/connectivity and for connector homogeneity combined with density, plus a weak separability factor. However, only two factors have eigenvalues above 1 and two were suggested, so Factors 3 and 4 should be read with caution; Density and Average connector degree cross-load on several factors, and Connector Mismatch remains unassigned due to low communality (0.21).
caveats: Four factors were extracted although two were suggested and the third and fourth eigenvalues (0.91, 0.71) are below 1, so the later factors may be over-extracted.
Maximum connector degree has a communality at the bound (possible Heywood case), which makes Factor 2 less reliable.
Average connector degree and Density cross-load on two or three factors, so they do not clearly separate the dimensions.
Connector Mismatch is unassigned because of low communality, and Sequentiality and Control flow complexity were removed by the MSA filter, so these aspects are not represented.
Number of empty sequence flows was constant and removed, so concurrency between parallel splits and joins is not covered.
The factors describe shared variance in these 288 nets and depend on the discovery algorithms, rotation and factor count; they do not imply causal relations.
